title: Police claim no choice but to shoot in fatal 2009 shooting
article: A Calgary police "heat" team member said during a fatality inquiry Monday there was no alternative but to shoot a man at the Western Pride car wash in 2009.
The Calgary Herald reports the officer said Travis Douglas Oakes was warned to give himself up before continuing to attempt escape in a stolen vehicle.
He also said shooting out the tires was not an option because that wouldn't stop anyone who insists on fleeing and makes it dangerous other vehicles and pedestrians.
Oakes, who was wanted on warrants for 20 criminal charges, including dangerous driving, died of a head wound from the gun shots during the morning of March 18th.
During questioning, a couple of officers were asked about a text message from another police vehicle four hours earlier saying "we should just shoot him already."
An officer insisted there was no consideration of shooting Oakes at that point.
Sergeant Dave Jennings, who fired the fatal shots is scheduled to testify Wednesday.
